title: Personal Identity Information Collection During Account Registration
description: The homeowner's personal identification information (name, email, address, etc.) is collected during account registration, creating a risk of unauthorized identification and profiling.

title: Linkability of Homeowner Data Across Services
description: Data collected during account registration and device enrollment could be linked with other data sources (e.g., other smart home services, online platforms), enabling comprehensive profiling of the homeowner.

title: Disclosure of Home Security Configuration
description: Information about enrolled cameras and sensors reveals the homeowner's security setup, creating risks of targeted surveillance or security bypass attempts by malicious actors.

title: Account Impersonation During Device Enrollment
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the homeowner to enroll unauthorized devices or gain access to the home hub account, compromising system security.

title: Tampering with Device Enrollment Data
description: The Home Hub process could potentially have device enrollment data tampered with, allowing unauthorized devices to be added or legitimate devices to be removed from the system.

title: Guest access code linked to identity
description: The system may link the guest's temporary access code to their identity or other personal data, enabling profiling or tracking across sessions.

title: Access code disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The temporary access code may be logged, displayed, or transmitted in a way that allows unauthorized parties to observe or intercept it.

title: Unauthorized access via compromised code
description: If the temporary access code is shared or compromised, an unauthorized person could gain access to the home.

title: Disclosure of Sensitive Event Data
description: Motion/door/sensor events written to the local event log could reveal patterns of life, presence at home, and daily routines, potentially exposing sensitive information about occupants to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Event data is accessible beyond intended recipients

title: Data Integrity Compromise
description: The local event log could be tampered with or modified by unauthorized parties, compromising the integrity of the recorded events and potentially leading to false records of activities.
assumptions: Event log is not adequately protected from unauthorized modification

title: Identification of Individuals from Event Patterns
description: Analysis of motion/door/sensor events could potentially identify specific individuals based on unique patterns of movement, timing, and activity, even without explicit personal identifiers.
assumptions: Event patterns are distinctive enough to identify individuals

title: Linkability of Events to Individuals
description: Events could be linked to specific individuals and their activities, creating a comprehensive profile of behavior and presence that could be used for surveillance or profiling purposes.
assumptions: Events contain sufficient context to link to specific individuals

title: Potential Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: Collection and storage of motion/door/sensor events may violate privacy regulations if data retention policies are not properly implemented or if consent is not obtained for data collection.
assumptions: Data collection practices may not align with applicable privacy laws

title: Unauthorized Access to Cloud-Stored Video Clips
description: Cloud Video Storage (DS2) may be accessible by unauthorized parties who can view or download the uploaded camera clips without proper authentication or authorization controls.

title: Data Breach of Video Content
description: Cloud Video Storage (DS2) could suffer a security breach exposing video footage to third parties, potentially revealing sensitive information about home activities and occupants.

title: Identification of Individuals in Video Footage
description: Recorded camera clips uploaded to Cloud Video Storage (DS2) may contain identifiable images of individuals, including family members, visitors, or intruders, creating privacy risks.

title: Cloud Provider Access to Identifiable Video Data
description: Stored video data in Cloud Video Storage (DS2) could be accessed by cloud service providers or their employees, potentially leading to identification of individuals without consent.

title: Video Data Tampering
description: Uploaded video clips could be altered, deleted, or corrupted during storage in Cloud Video Storage (DS2), compromising the integrity of recorded evidence.

title: Data Integrity Compromise in Cloud Storage
description: Cloud Video Storage (DS2) may lack proper integrity controls, allowing unauthorized modification of video data before or after upload.

title: Linkability of Video Clips to Events
description: Uploaded camera clips could be linked to specific times, locations, or individuals, enabling correlation of video data with other information sources.

title: Cross-Reference Linkability of Stored Videos
description: Video data in Cloud Video Storage (DS2) could be linked with other datasets (e.g., user accounts, access logs) to create comprehensive profiles of individuals.

title: Unauthorized Home Hub Access
description: The Home Hub (P1) could be compromised, allowing attackers to intercept or manipulate video uploads before they reach Cloud Video Storage (DS2).

title: Cloud Storage Account Compromise
description: Cloud Video Storage (DS2) account credentials could be stolen, enabling unauthorized access to all stored video footage.

title: Linkability of Motion Alerts to User Identity
description: The real-time motion alert forwarded from Home Hub to Mobile App Backend could be linked to a specific user's identity and home location, enabling tracking of user presence and activities.
assumptions: The motion alert contains or can be correlated with user-specific data

title: Inference of User Occupancy Patterns
description: The mobile app backend receiving real-time motion alerts could enable inference of when users are home or away, revealing occupancy patterns that compromise privacy.
assumptions: Motion alerts are received and processed by the backend

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Motion Data
description: Motion alert data transmitted to the mobile app backend could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through backend compromise, data breach, or improper access controls.
assumptions: The backend has access to motion alert data

title: Excessive Data Collection via Real-time Motion Monitoring
description: Continuous real-time motion data collection by the Home Hub may exceed what is necessary for the stated purpose of security alerts, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The system collects motion data continuously rather than on-demand

title: Unauthorized disclosure of motion detection notification
description: The motion-detected notification could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission, revealing that motion was detected at the homeowner's property.

title: Linkability of motion detection data with other homeowner data
description: The motion-detected notification could be linked with other data about the homeowner, potentially revealing patterns of presence or activity at the property across different contexts.

title: Usurpation of homeowner identity for notification access
description: If authentication is weak, an attacker could potentially impersonate the homeowner to receive motion-detected notifications, gaining unauthorized access to property monitoring information.

title: Identification of homeowner through motion detection notification
description: The notification reveals that the homeowner is present at the property, which could be sensitive information that identifies the data subject's location and activity patterns.

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics shared with cloud vendor could potentially be linked to specific users or devices through cross-referencing with other data sources, enabling re-identification risks.
assumptions: Analytics data contains sufficient granularity or metadata that could enable linking across datasets.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: Cloud analytics vendor may share, sell, or disclose the aggregated device-usage analytics to unauthorized third parties without proper consent or contractual safeguards.
assumptions: Vendor lacks adequate data protection policies or contractual obligations to prevent unauthorized sharing.

title: Inference of User Behavior Patterns
description: Even aggregated analytics may reveal sensitive user behavior patterns, preferences, or usage habits that could be inferred and potentially misused.
assumptions: Analytics data contains behavioral indicators that could be analyzed to infer sensitive information about user groups.

title: Data Integrity Compromise During Storage
description: Cloud analytics vendor may alter, corrupt, or tamper with the aggregated device-usage analytics data during storage or processing, compromising data integrity.
assumptions: Vendor's security controls are insufficient to prevent unauthorized data modification.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance with Data Protection Laws
description: Sharing aggregated analytics with cloud vendor may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations if proper consent mechanisms, data minimization, or user rights are not maintained.
assumptions: Data sharing practices do not fully comply with applicable privacy regulations and user consent requirements.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Video Content During Transmission
description: Video clip data transmitted from cloud storage to mobile app backend could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Transmission channel is not fully encrypted or authentication is weak

title: Video Content Tampering During Transmission
description: Video clip data could be modified or corrupted during transmission from cloud storage to mobile app backend, compromising data integrity.
assumptions: Transmission channel lacks integrity verification mechanisms

title: Video Content Reveals Homeowner Identity and Location
description: Video content retrieved by mobile app backend could reveal the identity, location, or activities of the homeowner, leading to identification risks.
assumptions: Video contains identifiable visual information about the homeowner or their property

title: Video Data Linked to Other Personal Information
description: Video clip data could be linked to other personal data about the homeowner (e.g., name, address, contact info) through metadata or cross-referencing, increasing identifiability.
assumptions: Video metadata or associated data contains linking information

title: Unauthorized Access to Video Playback
description: Mobile app backend could be accessed by unauthorized users who impersonate the homeowner, allowing them to view video content they should not access.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are weak or compromised
